settingsPage.title: Settings
settingsPage.intro: The platform's own settings. Each game keeps its settings with it in the menu.

signIn.title: Sign-in providers
signIn.intro: Choose how people sign in. Any of these can be someone’s account; people link more on their connections page. Changes apply at once, no restart.
signIn.keySourceDefault: Saved secrets are encrypted with a built-in development key. Set SECRETS_KEY or SESSION_SECRET before you go live.
signIn.loadError: Could not load the sign-in providers
signIn.issuerUrlHelp: The address of your OpenID Connect realm or tenant. Auto Tournament reads its endpoints from /.well-known/openid-configuration.
signIn.buttonNameHelp: Shown as “Sign in with …” on the login page, e.g. your community or identity server.
signIn.secretUnreadable: The saved secret can no longer be decrypted (the encryption key changed). Enter it again.
signIn.callbackHint: Set automatically. Paste it as the redirect URL in {{provider}}'s developer settings:

testResult.invalid_credentials: The provider rejected these credentials. Check the client ID and secret (or the key).
testResult.unreachable: Could not reach the provider. Check the network and try again.
testResult.unexpected: The provider gave an answer the test does not understand.

signIn.welcomeTitle: Set up how players sign in
signIn.welcomeBody: You are signed in as the admin. Turn on at least one provider below (Steam, Discord, Google, GitHub or Twitch) so players can sign in.

adminAccess.title: Admin access
adminAccess.localLoginHelp: Username and password sign-in at /login/admin. If you lose access, run reset-admin on the server.
adminAccess.localLoginLocked: Stays on until another admin can sign in with a provider that is turned on.
adminAccess.steamIdsHelp: Steam64 IDs, separated by commas. Made admin when saved and at every start. Removing one does not take admin away.
adminAccess.emailsHelp: Addresses that get admin when their owner signs in with a provider that verified them (Google, Discord, GitHub).
adminAccess.loadError: Could not load the admin access settings
adminAccess.short: Who can sign in as an admin

signIn.short: How players and admins sign in. Changes apply at once.

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.short: Username and password accounts you create
accounts.help: People sign in with these at /login/admin. Give admin to the ones who run the site; the rest sign in as players.
accounts.usernameHelp: 3 to 32 characters: lower-case letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores.
accounts.name: Display name
accounts.nameHelp: Optional. Shown on the site; the username is used when left empty.
accounts.setPasswordTotp: Their two-step verification is turned off too; they set it up again after signing in.
accounts.removeBody: They can no longer sign in with this username and password, and they are no longer an admin. Their player, matches and stats stay; making the same username again gives them back.

signIn.oidcScopes: On your OpenID Connect server, give this client the scopes openid, profile and email (in Keycloak: Clients → this client → Client scopes, with profile and email as Default). Without profile and email people still sign in, but the platform gets no name or email address for them.

steam.title: Steam Integration
steam.apiKeyHelper: Resolves Steam vanity URLs and player info. Leave blank to disable lookups.
steam.statusOk: Steam API key is set and reachable.
steam.statusNotConfigured: Steam API key is not set. Vanity URLs cannot be resolved until you add a key.
steam.statusUnreachable: Steam API key appears set but Steam could not be reached. Check your network or key.
steam.statusError: Failed to check Steam API status. Please try again.

ratings.title: Rating Updates
ratings.description: Control whether completed matches update player Skill Ratings. Disable this for events where an external system (for example your Excel sheet) is the source of truth for ratings.
ratings.toggleLabel: Update player ratings from completed matches
ratings.note: When disabled, all matches will still track stats (ADR, K/D, etc.), but player Skill Ratings will remain unchanged.

registration.title: Player registration
registration.description: Control whether signing in creates a player record for someone new, whichever sign-in method they use (Steam, Discord, Google and the others you enabled). When disabled, only players created or imported by admins appear in private tournaments and shuffle pools.
registration.toggleLabel: Allow anyone to register by signing in
registration.recommendation: Recommended: keep this off for invite‑only or private tournaments so random sign-ins do not fill up the player list.
registration.short: Signing in makes a player of anyone new. Off: only players you add.

players.title: Players
players.short: Who joins, and how ratings move.

developer.resetApiDescription: Danger zone: drops and recreates the entire database schema, then reinitializes default data (maps, map pools, etc.). Use only for local development. This is irreversible.
developer.resetApiSuccess: API and database reset successfully. All data has been wiped and defaults reinitialized.
developer.resetApiError: Failed to reset API and database. Check API logs for details.

resetApiDialog.title: Reset API & wipe all data?
resetApiDialog.description: This will drop and recreate the entire database schema. All tournaments, matches, players, teams, ratings, events, logs, and settings will be permanently deleted. This action cannot be undone. Continue?

site.saveFailed: Could not save the site name

experimental.title: Experimental
experimental.description: Features that are still being built. They are off by default and may change or break. Only admins see them.
experimental.envOverride: Set by the {{env}} environment variable. Change it there.
experimental.short: Still being built: off by default, only admins see them.

matchmaking.openDescription: On: every signed-in player sees Play and can queue. Off: only admins can find matches.
matchmaking.boardDescription: Off: only signed-in players see the matchmaking leaderboard. On: anyone with the link.
matchmaking.windowDescription: How far apart in rating players may be. It starts at the first number, grows by the step every 30 seconds up to the cap, and after the last number of minutes anyone is matched (leave it empty for never).
matchmaking.reservedDescription: Tournament matches go first, but leave this many free servers for matchmaking while players are searching. 0 = none.
matchmaking.modesDescription: What players can search. All modes are on by default. 1v1 is an aim duel.
matchmaking.poolsDescription: The map pool each mode picks from (Maps page; Workshop maps work too). The match room shows a roulette over the pool before revealing the map.
matchmaking.title: Matchmaking
matchmaking.short: Always on. Players find a match, queue and accept, then play on a free server.
matchmaking.saveFailed: Could not save the matchmaking settings
matchmaking.loadFailed: Could not load the matchmaking settings

license.title: License
license.getKey: Already have a license? Copy your key from <consoleLink>the Auto Tournament console</consoleLink>. Need one? <pricingLink>See pricing</pricingLink>.
license.useFromPaidKey: Set by the paid license key below.
license.useFromFreeKey: Set by the free key below: non-profit use only.
license.useWithoutKey: No key: free for non-profit use. Paste a paid key below for commercial use.
license.publicLine: Players see “{{line}}” at the bottom of event pages.
license.pageIntro: Your license key and where it stands. A paid key is for commercial use; a free key is for non-profit use.
license.description: Paste your Auto Tournament license key: a paid one for commercial use, or a free one for non-profit use. It is checked on this server, and once a day with autotournament.gg.
license.loadFailed: Could not read the license status.
license.none: No license key yet. Free for non-profit use; commercial use needs a paid license.
license.invalid: This key could not be verified.
license.invalidShort: The saved key could not be verified.
license.warningsNote: Nothing is blocked or limited. This is only a notice.
license.label: License key
license.helper: Starts with ATL1. Copy it from <consoleLink>your licenses in the Auto Tournament console</consoleLink>. After saving, only the license ID is shown.
license.checkInNote: Without a license key, nothing is sent to Auto Tournament. With a key, this server checks in once a day with the key's id and its server count.
license.saveFailed: Could not save the license key
license.removeFailed: Could not remove the license key

badge.label: Show "Licensed" and the kind of use on public event pages
badge.note: Off by default. Links to the license's public check page, and only shows while the saved key is valid.
badge.failed: Could not change the public license line
badge.short: On by itself once a key is saved. Players see it at the bottom of event pages.
badge.needsKey: Shows only with a license key saved, free or paid. Save one above first.

consent.title: One last thing: the license
consent.subtitle: Sorry, one more step and then you're done. Auto Tournament is free if nobody earns money from it; if someone does, you need a license. Skim the short version, pick how you use it, and type I AGREE.
consent.intro: Auto Tournament is source-available under the {{name}}. In short:

points.free: Free for personal use, hobby projects, learning, and events where nobody earns money from it.
points.orgs: Free for charities, schools, universities, public research and government bodies, even when they charge entry.
points.commercial: Commercial use needs a license. That includes paid hosting, selling it or a service built on it, events that make a profit, use inside a business, and being paid to set it up for someone.
points.servers: Every game server counts toward the license.
points.nothingLocked: Nothing is locked or limited without a key. You can add a key now or later.
points.forks: You can change the code and share it. Keep the license with it; the same rules apply.

consent.summaryNote: This is a short summary, and the text in your version may be out of date. The current license and licensing rules are on autotournament.gg — if they differ from this summary, they win.
consent.privacyNote: Your answer is saved on this server only. Without a license key, nothing is sent to Auto Tournament. With a key, this server checks in once a day with the key's id and its server count.

use.noncommercialHint: Free. Nobody earns money from it.
use.commercialHint: You need a license. Paste your key now or later.

consent.keyHelper: Starts with ATL1. Copy it from <consoleLink>your licenses in the Auto Tournament console</consoleLink>, or add it later in Settings > License.
consent.confirmLabel: Type {{phrase}} to accept the license terms
consent.confirmHelper: By typing {{phrase}} you accept the license terms for this instance.
consent.termsChanged: The license terms changed since they were last accepted. Please read them and accept again.
consent.onlyAdmins: Only admins see this, once per instance. Players, public pages and running matches are not affected.
consent.changeTitle: Change how this instance is used
consent.changeNote: Choose again and type I AGREE. The change is saved with the date and your account.
consent.commercialNoKey: This instance is used commercially, so you need a license. Copy your key from <consoleLink>your licenses in the Auto Tournament console</consoleLink> and paste it below. Nothing is locked while it is missing.

checkin.never: No license check-in yet. The first one runs shortly after a key is saved.
checkin.intro: Once a day, and only while a key is saved, this server sends:
checkin.keyId: The license key, so its id and signature can be checked
checkin.instanceId: A random id for this installation, made once
checkin.activity: Counts since the last check-in: finished matches, tournaments with activity, and the largest team count
checkin.declared: Your answer to the event dates question, if you gave one
checkin.notSent: No names, addresses, players or match details.

eventPrompt.title: Planning something new?
eventPrompt.body: Your event license covers {{dates}}. Let us know if you're testing, have a new event, or your dates moved — no action needed while you're testing.

warning.periodEnded: This event license covered dates up to {{date}}. Testing and setting up need no action; a new event gets its own event license.
warning.periodNotStarted: This event license covers dates from {{date}}. Setting up and testing before then is fine.

license.short: How this install is used, and its key.
license.thirdParty: This app is built with open-source packages under their own licenses.

tournamentsPage.liveShared: {{count}} live, sharing the servers. Matches get a server in the order they became ready.
tournamentsPage.empty: No tournaments yet. Create the first one.
tournamentsPage.deleteMessage: {{name}} and its matches, results and stats are deleted. This cannot be undone.

playedMatches.none: No matches have been played yet.

importMatch.title: Import a match
importMatch.subtitle: Add a match played somewhere else from its demos. The teams, players and score are read from the demos, then the match gets stats, a 2D replay and highlights like any other.
importMatch.eventHelp: Optional, for example the event's name.
importMatch.filesHelp: One CS2 demo (.dem) per map, in the order the maps were played.
importMatch.tooMany: Up to {{max}} demos, one per map.

state.failed: The demo could not be read

importMatch.doneAll: Imported. Highlights are recorded next if a highlight recorder is connected.
